cards.explanation: The answer is True. Matthew says Jesus went through all the towns and villages, "…teaching in their synagogues, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and sickness." Every disease and every sickness. I once fixed one crooked cookie and bragged about it for a week.

Jesus is moved with compassion because the crowds are harassed and helpless. Matthew says He was moved "…because they were harassed and helpless…" He saw what the crowds were carrying, and it moved Him.

The picture is sheep without a shepherd. The text says the crowds were harassed and helpless, "…like sheep without a shepherd." Sheep with no one to lead them don't have much of a plan. I can relate, friends, because I spent years stuck at the back of a junk drawer with no plan at all.
The answer is False. Jesus says, "The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few." So the harvest is big, and the workers are the part that's short. Lots to gather and not enough hands to do it.
The word is "ask." Jesus says, "Ask the Lord of the harvest, therefore, to send out workers into His harvest." Ask. Simple as that. The harvest belongs to the Lord, so the asking goes to Him.

Jesus gives them authority over unclean spirits. Matthew says Jesus "…gave them authority over unclean spirits, so that they could drive them out and heal every disease and sickness." The authority came from Him. Twelve disciples got handed something big.

The answer is True. The text says "James son of Zebedee, and his brother John…" Two names, one pair of brothers, right next to each other on the list. Just like Peter and his brother Andrew right before them.
The answer is "tax collector." The list says "…Matthew the tax collector…" Name and job in one breath, like a name tag at a work event. No small talk needed.
The list says Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus. It ends with "…Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus." That's a heavy way to end a list. I think it's a sad line, and the text doesn't say more here.
